PIT-001.q: How does PIT Law 109/2025/QH15 take effect and apply?
o: Effective 01/7/2026; provisions on business income and salary/wages of residents apply from the 2026 tax period
PIT-001.e: Law 109/2025/QH15 was passed on 10/12/2025 and takes effect on 01/7/2026; business income and employment income of residents apply from the 2026 tax period.
PIT-001.x:
Basis: PIT Law 109/2025/QH15 (passed 10/12/2025); Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Generally effective 01/07/2026, but the business and employment income rules for residents apply to the whole 2026 period, as these are finalised annually. Per-transaction income (transfers, winnings…) follows the new rules from 01/07/2026.
Distractors: B wrongly covers all income; C and D have wrong dates.

PIT-002.q: The decree detailing the 2025 PIT Law, effective 01/7/2026 and replacing Decree 65/2013/ND-CP, is:
PIT-002.e: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP guides PIT; 252/2026 guides the Tax Administration Law; 254/2026 covers invoices and vouchers; 320/2025 covers CIT.
PIT-002.x:
Basis: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Decree 253/2026 details the 2025 PIT Law, replacing Decree 65/2013. Distinguish the companion decrees: 252/2026 – tax administration; 254/2026 – invoices and documents (including PIT withholding certificates); 320/2025 – CIT.

PIT-003.q: Select ALL cases in which an individual is a tax resident:
o: Present in Vietnam 183 days or more in a calendar year
Present in Vietnam 183 days or more in 12 consecutive months from the first day of presence
Has a regular residence in Vietnam (permanent registration or a rented home as prescribed)
Has a bank account in Vietnam
Has a labour contract with a Vietnamese company but works entirely abroad and has never been in Vietnam
PIT-003.e: Residents: present 183 days or more in a calendar year or 12 consecutive months, or have a regular residence in Vietnam. Bank accounts or labour contracts are not residence criteria.
PIT-003.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: A person is resident if any condition holds: (A) present 183 days or more in a calendar year; (B) 183 days within 12 consecutive months from first arrival; (C) a habitual residence (permanent registration or rented housing as regulated).
Distractors: (D) A bank account and (E) an employment contract aren't residency tests; someone never present in Vietnam can't be resident.

PIT-004.q: Residents pay PIT on income arising inside and outside Vietnam; non-residents pay only on income arising in Vietnam.
PIT-004.e: True. This is the scope principle by residence status.
PIT-004.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Residents are taxed on worldwide income (with treaty credits for foreign tax); non-residents only on Vietnam-source income, wherever paid.

PIT-005.q: Employment income of a NON-resident is taxed at:
o: A flat 20% on taxable income, with no family deductions
10% on the portion above VND 5 million
PIT-005.e: Non-residents: tax = taxable employment income × 20%, no family deductions.
PIT-005.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Non-residents: tax = employment income × 20% flat, with no family deductions and no annual finalisation.
Distractors: B is for residents; C confuses it with 10% withholding on casual income; D has no basis.

PIT-006.q: Non-residents are not entitled to family deductions on employment income.
PIT-006.e: True. Family deductions apply only to residents.
PIT-006.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Family deductions (self and dependants) apply only to residents, as they relate to tax on total income and family obligations in Vietnam.

PIT-007.q: The PIT period for residents' employment income is:
o: Annual (withholding/provisional payments during the year and annual finalisation)
PIT-007.e: Residents' employment income has an annual tax period; tax is withheld/paid provisionally during the year and finalised at year-end.
PIT-007.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Residents' employment income has an annual tax period: employers withhold monthly, then finalise to correct differences (multiple employers, deduction changes…).
Distractors: B is for non-residents and casual income; C and D skip finalisation.

PIT-008.q: How many brackets does the progressive schedule for residents' employment income have under Law 109/2025/QH15?
PIT-008.e: Law 109/2025/QH15 reduced the schedule from 7 to 5 brackets from the 2026 tax period.
PIT-008.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The progressive schedule shrinks from 7 brackets (5%–35%) to 5 (5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 35%) from 2026 – dropping 15% and 25% and widening each bracket.
Distractors: 7 brackets is the old schedule; 6 and 4 have no basis.

PIT-009.q: For income paid from 01/01/2026 to before 01/7/2026, payers that filed under the old rules need not refile monthly/quarterly returns; differences are adjusted at the 2026 finalisation.
PIT-009.e: True. The transitional rule in Decree 253/2026/ND-CP avoids refiling; differences are settled at the 2026 finalisation.
PIT-009.x:
Basis: Transitional provisions of Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. In H1 2026 employers withheld under the old rules (7 brackets, 11 million deduction) and needn't amend monthly/quarterly returns. At the 2026 finalisation, the new schedule and deductions apply to the whole year, with overpayments offset or refunded.

PIT-010.q: The family deduction of VND 15.5 million/month applies only to income from July 2026 when Law 109/2025/QH15 takes effect.
PIT-010.e: False. Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15 applies the new deductions from the 2026 tax period, i.e., the whole of 2026 (from 01/01/2026).
PIT-010.x:
Basis: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15 adjusting family deductions.
Analysis: False. The new deductions (15.5 million for self, 6.2 million per dependant) apply from the 2026 period – all 12 months – without waiting for Law 109/2025's 01/07/2026 effective date.

PIT-011.q: Match monthly assessable income with the rate under the progressive schedule from the 2026 tax period:
PIT-011.e: The 5-bracket schedule under Law 109/2025/QH15. Annual equivalents: 120 – 360 – 720 – 1,200 million VND.
PIT-011.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: Monthly 5-bracket schedule: ≤ 10 million – 5%; > 10–30 – 10%; > 30–60 – 20%; > 60–100 – 30%; > 100 – 35%. Annual equivalents ×12: 120 – 360 – 720 – 1,200 million.
Note: Apply it to taxable income (after deductions), not gross salary.

PIT-012.q: The personal deduction for the taxpayer from the 2026 tax period is:
PIT-012.e: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15: VND 15.5 million/month (186 million/year), up from 11 million.
PIT-012.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: Personal deduction is 15.5 million/month (186 million/year), up from 11 million (Resolution 954/2020).
Distractors: 11 million is the old level; 13 and 17 million have no basis.

PIT-013.q: The deduction for each dependant from the 2026 tax period is:
PIT-013.e: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15: VND 6.2 million/month per dependant, up from 4.4 million.
PIT-013.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: Each dependant deduction is 6.2 million/month (74.4 million/year), up from 4.4 million.
Distractors: 4.4 million is the old level; 5.5 and 7 million have no basis.

PIT-014.q: Under the new schedule, the top 35% rate applies to monthly assessable income above VND 100 million (previously above 80 million).
PIT-014.e: True. The top bracket threshold rose from 80 to 100 million per month.
PIT-014.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: True. 35% now applies above 100 million/month of taxable income instead of above 80 million – easing the burden on upper-middle earners.

PIT-015.q: A resident's assessable employment income for March 2026 is VND 8 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-015.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: 8 million is in bracket 1 (≤ 10 million): 8,000,000 × 5% = 400,000 VND.

PIT-016.q: A resident's monthly assessable employment income is VND 25 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-016.e: Bracket 1: 10 million × 5% = 0.5 million; bracket 2: 15 million × 10% = 1.5 million. Total 2,000,000 VND (or 25 × 10% − 0.5 = 2 million).
PIT-016.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: Bracket 1: 10 × 5% = 0.5 million; bracket 2: (25 − 10) × 10% = 1.5 million. Total 2,000,000 VND. Check: 25 × 10% − 0.5 = 2 million.
Note: Multiplying all 25 million by 10% (2.5 million) is wrong for a progressive schedule.

PIT-017.q: A resident's monthly assessable employment income is VND 75 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-017.e: 0.5 + 2 + 6 + (75 − 60) × 30% = 13 million. Shortcut for bracket 4: 30% × income − 9.5 million = 22.5 − 9.5 = 13,000,000 VND.

PIT-018.q: A resident's monthly assessable employment income is VND 100 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-018.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: 10 × 5% + 20 × 10% + 30 × 20% + 40 × 30% = 0.5 + 2 + 6 + 12 = 20.5 million VND. Check: 30% × 100 − 9.5 = 20.5.
Note: 100 million is still bracket 4 (above 60 up to 100); 35% applies only above 100 million.

PIT-019.q: Match each bracket with the shortcut formula for monthly tax (TI: assessable income, VND million):
PIT-019.e: Shortcut formulas derived from the 5-bracket schedule; they equal the bracket-by-bracket sum.
PIT-019.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: The subtracted constant accumulates rate differences at each threshold. B2: 10 × (10% − 5%) = 0.5. B3: 0.5 + 30 × (20% − 10%) = 3.5. B4: 3.5 + 60 × 10% = 9.5. B5: 9.5 + 100 × 5% = 14.5.

PIT-020.q: April 2026: an employee earns VND 30 million (fully taxable), pays compulsory insurance of 10.5% on 30 million and has 1 registered dependant. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-020.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: Compulsory insurance = 30 × 10.5% = 3.15 million. Taxable income = 30 − 3.15 − 15.5 (self) − 6.2 (1 dependant) = 5.15 million. Tax = 5.15 × 5% = 257,500 VND.

PIT-021.q: August 2026: a department head earns VND 60 million (fully taxable), compulsory insurance VND 5.4 million, no dependants. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-021.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: Taxable income = 60 − 5.4 − 15.5 = 39.1 million (bracket 3). Tax = 20% × 39.1 − 3.5 = 4.32 million = 4,320,000 VND.
Note: Insurance of 5.4 million is below 10.5% × 60 because of the contribution salary cap.

PIT-022.q: A resident's 2026 annual assessable employment income is VND 480 million. What is the annual PIT (VND)?

PIT-023.q: A taxpayer has 2 dependants registered for all 12 months of 2026. What is the total annual family deduction (VND)?
PIT-023.x:
Basis: PIT Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15 (family deductions from tax year 2026 – per the question).
Working: Monthly deduction = self 15.5 million + 2 dependants × 6.2 million = 27.9 million; annual = 27.9 × 12 = 334.8 million = 334,800,000 VND.
Analysis: Dependants must be registered with supporting documents; deductions start from the month the support obligation arises. Each dependant can be claimed by only one taxpayer.
Note: The 15.5/6.2 million levels follow Resolution 110/2025 – check the original on the effective date.

PIT-024.q: Select ALL who may be registered as dependants (when conditions are met):
o: Children 18 or older who are disabled and unable to work
Parents outside working age whose average monthly income does not exceed the prescribed level
An elder brother working with income of VND 20 million/month
A 25-year-old child working with a stable income
PIT-024.e: Dependants include minor children, disabled children unable to work and relatives outside working age or unable to work with income within the limit; people with high income do not qualify.
PIT-024.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Dependants include (A) children under 18; (B) adult children with disabilities unable to work; (C) parents and relatives outside working age or unable to work with average monthly income within the limit (3 million – PIT-025).
Distractors: (D) a brother earning 20 million and (E) a 25-year-old with steady income fail the income/ability tests.

PIT-025.q: Under Decree 253/2026/ND-CP, the income condition for a dependant is average monthly income from all sources in the year:
o: Not exceeding the regional minimum wage
PIT-025.e: The dependant income threshold rose from VND 1 million to VND 3 million per month.
PIT-025.x:
Basis: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The dependant income limit rose from 1 million to 3 million/month (annual average, all sources), reflecting current incomes and living costs.
Distractors: 1 million is the old limit; 5 million and the regional minimum wage have no basis.

PIT-026.q: Each dependant can be deducted only once, for one taxpayer, in the same tax year.
PIT-026.e: True. For example, spouses must agree on which one claims the child.
PIT-026.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: True. A dependant can be claimed by only one taxpayer per year. Working spouses must agree who claims the child; choosing the higher marginal-rate spouse saves more.

PIT-027.q: The dependant deduction is counted from the month the support obligation arises.
PIT-027.e: True. For example, a child born in May is deductible from May (once registered).
PIT-027.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: True. Dependant deductions start from the month the support obligation arises (e.g., a child born in May → from May), once registered. Late registration within the year is corrected at finalisation.

PIT-028.q: For the same assessable income of VND 40 million/month, tax under the new 5-bracket schedule is lower than under the old 7-bracket schedule.
PIT-028.e: True. Old schedule: 6.75 million; new: 20% × 40 − 3.5 = 4.5 million VND.
PIT-028.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: Old schedule (b6: 25% × TI − 3.25) = 6.75 million. New (b3: 20% × TI − 3.5) = 4.5 million. The new tax is 2.25 million/month lower → true.

PIT-029.q: From the 2026 tax period, all night-work and overtime pay (compliant with labour law) of residents is PIT-exempt, not just the premium over day-time/normal-hours pay.
PIT-029.e: True. Law 109/2025/QH15 exempts the whole of night and overtime pay (previously only the premium).
PIT-029.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Previously only the premium above daytime/regular pay was exempt. From 2026, all night and overtime pay compliant with the Labour Code is exempt – simpler and supportive of production workers.
Note: Keep timesheets and overtime approvals within legal limits.

PIT-030.q: Night work under the Labour Code is from:
PIT-030.e: Night work is 22:00 to 06:00, the basis for identifying exempt night pay.
PIT-030.x:
Basis: Article 106 of Labour Code 45/2019/QH14.
Analysis: Night work runs from 22:00 to 06:00 – the basis for night pay (at least 30% extra) and its PIT exemption.
Distractors: The other time bands are wrong.

PIT-031.q: August 2026: a factory worker receives total pay of VND 24 million, of which 4 million is lawful overtime pay. Compulsory insurance 2.1 million; no dependants. What is the monthly assessable income (VND)?
PIT-031.e: All overtime pay is exempt: 24 − 4 − 2.1 − 15.5 = 2.4 million = 2,400,000 VND.
PIT-031.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Assessable = 24 − 4 (all overtime exempt) = 20 million. Taxable = 20 − 2.1 (insurance) − 15.5 (self) = 2.4 million VND.
Note: Under the old rule only the premium was exempt, so taxable income would be higher.

PIT-032.q: From 01/7/2026, mid-shift meal allowances paid in cash are excluded from PIT taxable income up to:
PIT-032.e: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP raised the limit from 730,000 to 1.2 million per month; the excess is taxable.
PIT-032.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: From 01/07/2026, cash meal allowances are excluded up to 1.2 million/person/month (previously 730,000 VND); any excess is taxable.
Distractors: 730,000 is the old level; 1.5 and 2 million have no basis.

PIT-033.q: If the company cooks, buys meal portions or issues meal vouchers for employees, the meal value is not taxable and there is no cap.
PIT-033.e: True. The 1.2 million cap applies only to cash payments.
PIT-033.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. When the employer cooks, buys meals or issues meal vouchers, the meal value isn't taxable and isn't capped. The 1.2 million cap applies only to cash allowances.
Note: For CIT, meal costs still need valid invoices.

PIT-034.q: September 2026: the company pays a cash meal allowance of VND 1.5 million per person. How much is taxable for each person (VND)?
PIT-034.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 1,500,000 − 1,200,000 = 300,000 VND taxable per person.

PIT-035.q: Pay for untaken annual leave days (within the labour law limits) is PIT-exempt.
PIT-035.e: True. Decree 253/2026/ND-CP exempts pay for untaken leave within the rules; any excess is taxable.
PIT-035.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; 2019 Labour Code (Articles 113–114).
Analysis: True. Pay for untaken annual leave (on termination or as regulated) within labour law limits is exempt; payment for days beyond the statutory entitlement is taxable.

PIT-036.q: Severance/job-loss allowances above the Labour Code levels are PIT-exempt if based on the company's financial regulations, internal rules, labour contract or collective agreement.
PIT-036.e: True. Without an internal basis, the excess over the statutory level is taxable.
PIT-036.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Severance and job-loss allowances under the Labour Code aren't taxable; amounts above that are exempt if backed by a financial policy, internal rules, employment contract or collective agreement. Otherwise, the excess is taxable.

PIT-037.q: Housing provided free by the enterprise (including electricity, water and related services) is not taxable for PIT.
PIT-037.e: True under Decree 253/2026/ND-CP. If the company pays rent on the employee's behalf, it is taxable but capped at 15% of total taxable income (excluding the rent).
PIT-037.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Free employer-provided housing (including utilities and services) isn't taxable. Different from rent paid on the employee's behalf: taxable, but capped at 15% of other taxable income (PIT-038).

PIT-038.q: A company pays VND 10 million/month rent on behalf of an expert; the expert's taxable employment income (excluding rent) is VND 40 million/month. How much rent is included in monthly taxable income (VND)?
PIT-038.e: Cap = 15% × 40 = 6 million (< 10 million actually paid), so 6,000,000 VND is included.
PIT-038.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Cap = 15% × 40 = 6 million < 10 million paid → 6,000,000 VND taxable.
Note: If actual rent is below 15%, the actual amount is used.

PIT-039.q: Select ALL items that are NOT taxable or are PIT-exempt:
o: Pensions paid by the social insurance fund
PIT-039.e: Cash Tet bonuses and position allowances are taxable employment income.
PIT-039.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Non-taxable/exempt: (A) compliant overtime and night pay; (B) social insurance pensions; (C) insurance indemnities; (D) scholarships.
Distractors: (E) Tet bonuses and (F) position allowances are taxable employment income.

PIT-040.q: 13th-month salary and cash Tet bonuses paid to employees are taxable employment income.
PIT-040.e: True. Performance-linked bonuses are taxable income.
PIT-040.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. 13th-month and Tet cash bonuses relate to employment, so they're taxable. Narrow exceptions cover certain State honours and prescribed awards.

PIT-041.q: Compulsory insurance contributions paid by employees (SI 8%, HI 1.5%, UI 1%) are deductible when determining PIT assessable income.
PIT-041.e: True. The employee's 10.5% is deducted before applying the schedule.
PIT-041.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The employee's compulsory contributions (social 8%, health 1.5%, unemployment 1% = 10.5%) are deducted before applying the schedule. The employer's share isn't employee income.

PIT-042.q: Under Decree 253/2026/ND-CP, the maximum deduction for voluntary pension fund contributions is:
PIT-042.e: The deduction for voluntary pension contributions rose from 1 million to 3 million per month.
PIT-042.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Voluntary pension contributions are deductible up to 3 million/month (up from 1 million) – encouraging retirement saving.
Distractors: 1 million is the old cap; 2 and 5 million have no basis.

PIT-043.q: The maximum deductions for medical and education/training expenses for residents (2026 tax period) are:
o: Medical up to VND 23 million/year; education/training up to VND 24 million/year
PIT-043.e: Medical costs within the health-insurance list at domestic facilities: up to 23 million/year; domestic education/training: up to 24 million/year (47 million in total).
PIT-043.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The new law adds deductions for medical costs (on the health insurance list, at domestic facilities) up to 23 million/year and domestic education/training up to 24 million/year – 47 million in total.
Distractors: B has wrong amounts; C removes the caps; D combines them wrongly.

PIT-044.q: Select ALL conditions for medical expenses to be deductible for PIT:
o: Incurred at a domestic medical facility
Within the list covered by health insurance
With invoices/documents in the name of the taxpayer or a dependant
Not yet paid by the health insurance fund, a sponsor or another source
Treatment at a foreign hospital with valid invoices
PIT-044.e: Only costs at domestic facilities, within the health-insurance list, properly documented and not covered by other sources are deductible.
PIT-044.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Four conditions: (A) at a domestic facility; (B) on the health insurance coverage list; (C) invoices in the name of the taxpayer or dependant; (D) not already paid by insurance or another source (no double benefit).
Distractors: (E) Foreign medical costs aren't deductible even with valid invoices.

PIT-045.q: Individuals who want medical/education deductions must finalise PIT directly with the tax authority and cannot authorise their employer to finalise for them.
PIT-045.e: True per the guidance in Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
PIT-045.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Medical and education deductions need the individual's own documents, so the individual must file directly; they fall outside employer-delegated finalisation (PIT-056).

PIT-046.q: Unused medical/education deductions in a year are carried forward to the next year.
PIT-046.e: False. Unused amounts cannot be carried forward.
PIT-046.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. Medical and education deductions are annual; unused amounts (insufficient income or above the cap) can't be carried forward.

PIT-047.q: Match each payment to employees with its PIT treatment (from 01/7/2026):
p: Rent paid by the company on the employee's behalf
Taxable, capped at 15% of total taxable income (excluding rent)
PIT-047.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Cash meal allowance – excluded up to 1.2 million/month (PIT-032); compliant overtime – fully exempt (PIT-029); 13th-month salary – fully taxable (PIT-040); rent paid on behalf – taxable up to 15% of other taxable income (PIT-038).

PIT-048.q: Charitable, humanitarian and study-promotion contributions to lawfully established organisations/funds (with documents) are deducted before calculating PIT on employment and business income.
PIT-048.e: True. Charity deductions apply with lawful documents.
PIT-048.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Charitable, humanitarian and education donations to lawfully established organisations or funds (with their receipts) are deducted from employment and business income. Gifts directly to individuals outside such organisations aren't deductible.

PIT-049.q: Business-trip and travel allowances paid within the company's financial regulations are not taxable income for employees.
PIT-049.e: True. They serve the work and are not employee income.
PIT-049.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Travel allowances within the company's financial policy are business costs, not personal benefits. Amounts above the policy or unsupported lump sums may be taxable income.

PIT-050.q: From 01/7/2026, payers must withhold 10% PIT on payments to residents without a labour contract or with a contract under 3 months when each payment is at least:
PIT-050.e: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP raised the 10% withholding threshold from VND 2 million to VND 5 million per payment.
PIT-050.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: From 01/07/2026, payments to residents without an employment contract or with one under 3 months require 10% withholding when each payment is 5 million or more (previously 2 million).
Distractors: 2 million is the old threshold; 10 and 1 million have no basis.

PIT-051.q: On 10/8/2026 a company pays VND 8 million as a technical consulting fee to a freelance expert (no labour contract, no commitment form). How much PIT must be withheld (VND)?
PIT-051.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Paid on 10/08/2026 (after 01/07/2026), 8 million ≥ 5 million, no commitment form → 10%: 8,000,000 × 10% = 800,000 VND.
Note: The payer issues an electronic withholding certificate (PIT-060).

PIT-052.q: After 01/7/2026, a payment of VND 4 million to an individual without a labour contract is not subject to mandatory 10% withholding.
PIT-052.e: True. Below 5 million per payment, withholding is not mandatory; the individual remains responsible for finalisation if required.
PIT-052.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. 4 million < 5 million per payment, so withholding isn't mandatory. The income is still taxable; the individual must finalise if total income exceeds the tax-free level. Payers mustn't split payments to avoid the threshold.

PIT-053.q: An individual with only casual income, whose estimated total income after family deductions is below the taxable level, may submit a commitment form so the payer temporarily does not withhold 10%.
PIT-053.e: True. The individual is responsible for the commitment's accuracy; the payer keeps it on file.
PIT-053.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. An individual with only casual income, estimating total income after deductions below the taxable level, may submit a commitment form to avoid 10% withholding. The individual answers for its truthfulness; the payer keeps it on file.

PIT-054.q: For employees with labour contracts of 3 months or more, payers withhold PIT using:
PIT-054.e: Contracts of 3 months or more: withhold using the progressive schedule after family deductions, compulsory insurance, etc.
PIT-054.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Employees with contracts of 3 months or more are withheld under the progressive schedule after family, insurance, pension and charity deductions – as regular, annually finalised income.
Distractors: B is for contracts under 3 months/no contract; C is for non-residents; D is wrong as employers must withhold.

PIT-055.q: Select ALL payments subject to 10% PIT withholding (from 01/7/2026):
o: VND 6 million fee for a trainer without a labour contract
VND 7 million/month wage for a seasonal worker on a 2-month contract
Monthly salary of an employee on a 1-year contract
VND 5 million commission per payment to a referral collaborator (no labour contract)
PIT-055.e: Payments of VND 5 million or more to individuals without a contract or with contracts under 3 months: 10%. 1-year contracts use the progressive schedule; dividends are withheld at 5%.
PIT-055.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: 10% withholding: (A) a 6 million fee, no employment contract; (B) a 2-month seasonal worker at 7 million/month; (E) a 5 million commission (meets 'from 5 million').
Distractors: (C) A 1-year contract uses the progressive schedule; (D) dividends are withheld at 5% (investment income).

PIT-056.q: An individual may authorise the income payer to finalise PIT on their behalf when:
o: They have a labour contract of 3 months or more with that payer and are working there at the time of authorisation (not claiming medical/education deductions)
They have any income from the payer
They have only casual income withheld at 10%
They work at several places on long-term contracts
PIT-056.e: Authorisation requires a labour contract of 3 months or more with the current payer. Those claiming medical/education deductions must self-finalise.
PIT-056.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Delegation requires a contract of 3 months or more with the payer and current employment there at delegation; minor withheld casual income may still allow delegation. Those claiming medical or education deductions must self-file (PIT-045).
Distractors: B is too broad; C – casual income alone doesn't qualify; D – multiple long-term employers require self-filing.

PIT-057.q: The deadline for an income payer's 2026 PIT finalisation for employment income is:
PIT-057.e: Payers finalise by the last day of the third month after the calendar year-end.
PIT-057.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Payers finalise by the last day of the third month after the calendar year → 31/03/2027 (same as the CIT finalisation).
Distractors: B is the individual self-filing deadline; C and D are wrong.

PIT-058.q: The deadline for individuals finalising PIT directly with the tax authority is:
o: The last day of the fourth month after the calendar year-end (next working day if a holiday)
The last day of the third month
PIT-058.e: Individuals self-finalise by the last day of the fourth month after year-end; if a holiday, the next working day.
PIT-058.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Individuals self-file by the last day of the fourth month after the year (30/04); as 30/04 is usually a holiday, it shifts to the next working day.
Distractors: B is the payer's deadline; C and D have no basis.

PIT-059.q: Payers of salary/wages must finalise PIT on behalf of authorising individuals and for themselves, even if no tax was withheld in the year.
PIT-059.e: True. The payer's finalisation duty does not depend on whether any tax was withheld.
PIT-059.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Employers must finalise for themselves and on behalf of delegating individuals, even with no withholding in the year – the return also serves as income data for the tax authority.

PIT-060.q: From 01/7/2026, income payers issue electronic PIT withholding certificates under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
PIT-060.e: True. Decree 254/2026/ND-CP replaces Decree 123/2020/ND-CP on e-invoices and e-vouchers, including PIT withholding certificates.
PIT-060.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP (replacing Decree 123/2020/ND-CP).
Analysis: True. From 01/07/2026, PIT withholding certificates are electronic under Decree 254/2026, letting the tax authority match withholding data with individuals' returns.

PIT-061.q: In 2026 an employee has total taxable salary of VND 480 million; compulsory insurance paid VND 30 million; no dependants. What is the annual PIT (VND)?
PIT-061.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Personal deduction = 15.5 × 12 = 186 million. Taxable = 480 − 30 − 186 = 264 million. Tax = 120 × 5% + (264 − 120) × 10% = 6 + 14.4 = 20.4 million VND.

PIT-062.q: In 2026 an employee has taxable salary of VND 480 million; compulsory insurance paid 30 million; 1 dependant registered for all 12 months. What is the annual PIT (VND)?
PIT-062.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Deductions = 186 + 6.2 × 12 = 260.4 million. Taxable = 480 − 30 − 260.4 = 189.6 million. Tax = 6 + (189.6 − 120) × 10% = 12.96 million VND.
Note: Versus PIT-061, one dependant saves 7.44 million (= 74.4 × 10% marginal rate).

PIT-063.q: Arrange the steps to calculate monthly PIT for an employee with a contract of 3 months or more:
o: Subtract family deductions, compulsory insurance, voluntary pension, charity
PIT-063.e: Assessable income = taxable income − deductions; then apply the 5-bracket schedule.
PIT-063.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Sequence: gross income → remove exempt/non-taxable items (overtime, meals within limit…) → assessable income → less family, insurance, pension and charity deductions → taxable income → progressive schedule.
Note: Swapping steps 2 and 3 doesn't change the arithmetic but misstates 'assessable income' on the return.

PIT-064.q: In 2026, payers still apply the 11 million/month family deduction for the first half and 15.5 million for the second half at finalisation.
PIT-064.e: False. 15.5 million and 6.2 million apply to the whole 2026 tax period; first-half withholding differences are settled at finalisation.
PIT-064.x:
Basis: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: False. At the 2026 finalisation, 15.5 and 6.2 million apply to all 12 months. H1 withholding at 11 million was provisional; the difference (usually an overpayment) is settled at finalisation (PIT-009).

PIT-065.q: Match each income type with the residents' PIT rate:
p: 10% on the portion above VND 20 million per time
5% on the portion above VND 20 million per time
PIT-065.e: Flat rates by income type; the threshold for winnings, royalties, franchising, inheritances and gifts rose to 20 million per time from 01/7/2026.
PIT-065.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Flat rates by income type: dividends 5% of income; securities 0.1% of each sale price; real estate 2% of the transfer price; winnings 10% above 20 million per win; royalties 5% above 20 million per payment.

PIT-066.q: From 01/7/2026, the per-time threshold for taxing winnings, royalties, franchising, inheritances and gifts is the portion above:
PIT-066.e: Law 109/2025/QH15 raised the threshold from 10 million to 20 million per time.
PIT-066.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: From 01/07/2026, the per-event threshold for winnings, royalties, franchising, inheritances and gifts rose from 10 to 20 million; tax applies only to the excess.
Distractors: 10 million is the old threshold; 5 and 50 million have no basis.

PIT-067.q: September 2026: an individual wins a promotional prize worth VND 50 million. What PIT is payable (VND)?
PIT-067.x:
Basis: PIT Law 109/2025/QH15 (prize income – per the question).
Working: Tax = (prize value − 20 million exempt portion) × 10% = (50 − 20) × 10% = 3 million = 3,000,000 VND.
Analysis: Prize income is taxed per receipt at a flat 10% on the excess over the threshold; the payer withholds before handing over the prize. No family deductions or annual finalisation apply.
Note: The 20 million threshold follows Law 109/2025 (10 million under the old law) – the question's basis; check the original.

PIT-068.q: August 2026: an individual inherits shares worth VND 120 million from someone not in an exempt relationship. What PIT is payable (VND)?
PIT-068.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: (120 − 20) × 10% = 10,000,000 VND.
Note: Inheritances from parents, spouses, grandparents or siblings may be exempt (real estate – PIT-072; check rules for other assets).

PIT-069.q: An individual shareholder receives cash dividends of VND 30 million. How much PIT is withheld (VND)?
PIT-069.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: Cash dividends are investment income at 5%: 30,000,000 × 5% = 1,500,000 VND, withheld by the payer.
Note: Stock dividends are taxed only when the shares are sold.

PIT-070.q: An individual sells listed shares for a total price of VND 500 million. What is the PIT (VND)?
PIT-070.e: 500,000,000 × 0.1% = 500,000 VND (on each transfer price, regardless of gain or loss).
PIT-070.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: 500,000,000 × 0.1% = 500,000 VND on each sale price, regardless of gain or loss; withheld by the broker.

PIT-071.q: An individual transfers a land plot (not exempt) for VND 3 billion. What is the PIT (VND)?
PIT-071.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: 3,000,000,000 × 2% = 60,000,000 VND.
Note: The transfer price can't be below the provincial land price table at the time.

PIT-072.q: Income from transfers, inheritances or gifts of real estate between spouses; parents and children; grandparents and grandchildren; and siblings is PIT-exempt.
PIT-072.e: True. This exemption is retained in Law 109/2025/QH15.
PIT-072.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Transfers, inheritances and gifts of real estate between spouses; parents and children (natural, adoptive, in-law); grandparents and grandchildren; and siblings are exempt – carried over from the old law.

PIT-073.q: Income from transferring an individual's only house/residential land in Vietnam is PIT-exempt when conditions are met.
PIT-073.e: True. Specific conditions are set by the Government.
PIT-073.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Transferring one's only residential house or land is exempt when Government conditions are met (e.g., minimum ownership period, transfer of the whole).

PIT-074.q: PIT on transfers of gold bars under Law 109/2025/QH15 is:
o: 0.1% of each transfer price; the Government sets the value threshold and start date
PIT-074.e: Law 109/2025/QH15 adds 0.1% of each transfer price for gold bars; the Government sets the threshold and timing.
PIT-074.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: The new law adds 0.1% tax on each sale price of gold bars; the Government sets the taxable value threshold and start date – to monitor gold trading without disrupting the market.
Distractors: B confuses it with real estate; C with non-residents; D is wrong as it is now taxable.

PIT-075.q: Income from transferring digital assets is subject to PIT at 0.1% of each transfer price.
PIT-075.e: True. Law 109/2025/QH15 adds digital assets to taxable income at 0.1%.
PIT-075.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Digital assets (as defined by the Digital Technology Industry Law) are now subject to PIT; transfers are taxed at 0.1% of each sale price – like securities.

PIT-076.q: Select ALL income newly made PIT-taxable by Law 109/2025/QH15 (5% on the portion above VND 20 million per time):
o: Transfer of auctioned vehicle number plates
Transfer of emission-reduction results/carbon credits (except exempt first transfers)
PIT-076.e: Deposit interest and remittances remain exempt.
PIT-076.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: The new law makes certain newly valuable rights taxable (5% above 20 million per event): (A) '.vn' domain names; (B) auctioned licence plates; (C) emission reductions and carbon credits (except the exempt first transfer – PIT-081).
Distractors: (D) Deposit interest and (E) remittances remain exempt (PIT-079).

PIT-077.q: An individual transfers an auctioned vehicle number plate with income of VND 120 million. What is the PIT (VND)?
PIT-077.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: (120 − 20) × 5% = 5,000,000 VND.
Note: Check Decree 253/2026 on how taxable income is measured where the original auction price is known.

PIT-078.q: Income from transferring open-ended fund certificates is PIT-exempt if held for 2 years or more from purchase.
PIT-078.e: True. A policy to encourage long-term investment via open-ended funds.
PIT-078.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Redeeming open-ended fund units is exempt if held at least 2 years from purchase – encouraging long-term saving through funds rather than short-term trading.

PIT-079.e: Dividends are investment income taxed at 5%.
PIT-079.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Exempt: (A) bank deposit interest; (B) remittances; (C) Government bond interest; (D) insurance indemnities.
Distractors: (E) Dividends are investment income taxed at 5% (PIT-069).

PIT-080.q: A household directly raising dairy cows and selling unprocessed (or ordinarily pre-processed) raw milk is PIT-exempt on this income.
PIT-080.e: True. Income of individuals directly producing agricultural/livestock products sold unprocessed is exempt.
PIT-080.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Income of individuals directly farming, raising livestock or aquaculture who sell unprocessed or ordinarily pre-processed products is PIT-exempt – matching the VAT non-taxable status at the producer stage (VAT-002).

PIT-081.q: Individuals' income from the first transfer of GHG emission-reduction results, carbon credits, green bonds and green bond interest is PIT-exempt.
PIT-081.e: True. A new group of exemptions supporting green growth.
PIT-081.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. In parallel with CIT (CIT-036), the PIT Law exempts income from the first transfer of emission reductions, carbon credits and green bonds, and green bond interest – tools of green growth policy.

PIT-082.q: Income after CIT of an individual owner of a sole proprietorship or a single-member LLC owned by the individual is PIT-exempt.
PIT-082.e: True. This avoids double taxation of the same income.
PIT-082.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Profits of sole proprietorships and single-member LLCs owned by an individual have borne CIT; when withdrawn, they aren't taxed again under PIT (unlike dividends from JSCs and multi-member LLCs at 5%).

PIT-083.q: Match the business activity of a NON-resident individual with the tax rate on revenue:
p: Production, construction, transport and other business
PIT-083.e: Non-residents with business income in Vietnam pay tax as a percentage of revenue.
PIT-083.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Non-residents with business income in Vietnam pay on revenue: goods 1%; production, construction, transport and other 2%; services 5% – not on net income, as costs are hard to verify.

PIT-084.q: From the 2026 tax period, household/individual businesses with annual revenue of VND 1 billion or less do not pay PIT.
PIT-084.e: True. Law 09/2026/QH16 delegates the threshold to the Government; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP sets 1 billion (Law 109/2025/QH15 originally set 500 million).
PIT-084.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Law 09/2026/QH16; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Law 109/2025 originally set 500 million; Law 09/2026 delegated the threshold to the Government and Decree 141/2026 raised it to 1 billion from 2026 – aligned with the VAT threshold (VAT-009).

PIT-085.q: Under Law 109/2025/QH15, household/individual businesses with annual revenue above VND 3 billion pay PIT by the income method (revenue minus expenses) × rate and cannot choose the percentage-of-revenue method.
PIT-085.e: True. The percentage-of-revenue method is only an option for those with revenue not exceeding 3 billion.
PIT-085.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Law 09/2026/QH16; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Household businesses above 3 billion must use (revenue − costs) × rate (17% or 20% by size) – requiring full books. Only the 1–3 billion group may choose between percentage of revenue and the income method.

PIT-086.q: Mark True/False for each statement on PIT in 2026:
o: The progressive schedule has 5 brackets, top rate 35%
The dependant deduction is VND 4.4 million/month
Cash meal allowances are exempt up to VND 1.2 million/month from 01/7/2026
Bank deposit interest is taxed at 5%
The 10% withholding threshold for casual income is VND 5 million per payment from 01/7/2026
PIT-086.e: The dependant deduction is 6.2 million; deposit interest is exempt.
PIT-086.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – 5 brackets, top 35%. (2) False – dependant deduction is 6.2 million (4.4 million is old). (3) True – cash meals exempt up to 1.2 million. (4) False – deposit interest is exempt. (5) True – the 10% withholding threshold is 5 million per payment.

PIT-087.q: A construction company hires a seasonal site engineer (2-month contract) paying VND 12 million/month from August 2026. Select ALL correct statements:
o: The company withholds 10% on each payment: VND 1.2 million
If the engineer has only this income and expects to be below the taxable level, they may submit a commitment form to avoid withholding
The company must withhold using the progressive schedule like permanent staff
The engineer gets family deductions immediately when the company withholds 10%
PIT-087.e: Contracts under 3 months: 10% on payments of 5 million or more; a commitment form is possible if eligible. Family deductions are considered at finalisation.
PIT-087.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (A) True – a 2-month contract (< 3 months), 12 million ≥ 5 million → 10% = 1.2 million. (B) True – a commitment form is allowed if this is the only income and below the taxable level.
Distractors: (C) The progressive schedule applies only to contracts of 3 months or more; (D) family deductions are considered at annual finalisation.

PIT-088.q: An employee has monthly assessable salary (after deductions) of VND 9 million and receives an internal innovation bonus of VND 12 million in October 2026. What is October's PIT?
PIT-088.e: The internal bonus is added to monthly income: TI = 9 + 12 = 21 million. Tax = 10% × 21 − 0.5 = 1.6 million VND.
PIT-088.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: An internal innovation bonus is employment income added to the month paid: TI = 9 + 12 = 21 million (bracket 2). Tax = 10% × 21 − 0.5 = 1.6 million.
Distractors: B, C and D split the bonus or use the wrong bracket.

PIT-089.q: When an enterprise gives employees Tet gifts in kind (with invoices), the gift value is not taxable income.
PIT-089.e: False. In-kind benefits of a salary nature (other than prescribed exclusions) remain taxable.
PIT-089.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. In-kind Tet gifts are employment benefits taxable at their value (except specifically excluded items such as employer-provided meals, uniforms…). An invoice only matters for the company's CIT deduction.

PIT-090.q: A resident's monthly assessable employment income is VND 45 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-090.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: 45 million is bracket 3: 20% × 45 − 3.5 = 5.5 million. Check: 0.5 + 2 + (45 − 30) × 20% = 5.5 million VND.

PIT-091.q: A resident's monthly assessable employment income is VND 120 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-091.e: 35% × 120 − 14.5 = 27.5 million VND (20.5 million on the first 100 million + 20 × 35% = 7).
PIT-091.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: Bracket 5: 35% × 120 − 14.5 = 27.5 million. Check: 20.5 (first 100 million – PIT-018) + 20 × 35% = 27.5 million VND.

PIT-092.q: May 2026: an employee earns VND 40 million (fully taxable), compulsory insurance 4.2 million, 2 dependants. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-092.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: TI = 40 − 4.2 − 15.5 − 2 × 6.2 = 7.9 million (bracket 1). Tax = 7.9 × 5% = 395,000 VND.
Note: In May 2026 the employer may have withheld under old deductions; the difference is settled at finalisation (PIT-009).

PIT-093.q: September 2026: an employee receives salary of VND 20 million and a cash meal allowance of 1.5 million; compulsory insurance 2.1 million; no dependants. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-093.e: Taxable meal allowance: 1.5 − 1.2 = 0.3 million. TI = 20 + 0.3 − 2.1 − 15.5 = 2.7 million; tax = 135,000 VND.
PIT-093.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Excess meal allowance = 1.5 − 1.2 = 0.3 million (taxable). TI = 20 + 0.3 − 2.1 − 15.5 = 2.7 million. Tax = 2.7 × 5% = 135,000 VND.

PIT-094.q: A resident's 2026 annual assessable employment income is VND 900 million. What is the annual PIT (VND)?
PIT-094.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working (annual): 120 × 5% = 6; 240 × 10% = 24; 360 × 20% = 72; (900 − 720) × 30% = 54. Total 156 million. Check: 75 million/month → 13 × 12 = 156 (PIT-017).

PIT-095.q: An individual with employment income from several payers in a year gets the personal deduction (15.5 million/month) only once and cannot double-count it across payers at finalisation.
PIT-095.e: True. On self-finalisation, the total annual personal deduction is 186 million.
PIT-095.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: True. The personal deduction applies once a year (186 million). If both employers deduct 15.5 million/month, the individual must pay back the resulting shortfall at finalisation.

PIT-096.q: A resident with labour contracts of 3 months or more at two companies in the same year cannot authorise finalisation and must finalise directly with the tax authority.
PIT-096.e: True. Authorisation applies only with a 3-month-plus contract at one current employer (with limited exceptions for small casual income already withheld).
PIT-096.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Delegated finalisation requires a 3-month-plus contract with one current employer. With two concurrent long-term contracts, the individual must self-file to aggregate income and apply the right brackets.

PIT-097.q: Select ALL income arising after 01/7/2026 that is subject to PIT:
o: Inherited shares of VND 100 million from a non-exempt relationship
Savings deposit interest of VND 20 million
PIT-097.e: The first three exceed the 20 million per-time threshold; deposit interest and scholarships are exempt.
PIT-097.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Taxable: (A) 50 million lottery > 20 million → (50 − 20) × 10% = 3 million; (B) 30 million royalty → (30 − 20) × 5% = 0.5 million; (C) 100 million inheritance → (100 − 20) × 10% = 8 million.
Distractors: (D) Deposit interest and (E) scholarships are exempt.

PIT-098.q: August 2026: an author receives a one-off royalty of VND 50 million. What PIT is payable (VND)?
PIT-098.x:
Basis: PIT Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP (per the question) – royalty income.
Working: Tax = (royalty − 20 million) × 5% = (50 − 20) × 5% = 1.5 million = 1,500,000 VND.
Analysis: Royalty income (transfer or licensing of IP rights) is taxed per contract at 5% on the excess over the threshold; the payer withholds before payment. It differs from fees for commissioned work (usually treated as employment/casual income).
Note: Decree 253/2026 is a 2026 text beyond my knowledge; the explanation follows the question's basis.

PIT-099.q: October 2026: an individual receives shares worth VND 30 million as a gift from a friend. What PIT is due on the gift (VND)?
PIT-099.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: A gift of shares from a non-exempt person (a friend): (30 − 20) × 10% = 1,000,000 VND.
Note: Gifts within the exempt family circle (PIT-072) aren't taxed.

PIT-100.q: Premiums for savings-type (non-compulsory) life insurance bought by the enterprise for employees are taxable income of the employees.
PIT-100.e: True. The enterprise must withhold tax on these premiums as prescribed.
PIT-100.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Accumulating life insurance premiums paid by the employer give employees a financial benefit, so they're taxable; the employer withholds as regulated (e.g., 10% of premiums). Unlike non-accumulating cover (PIT-121).

PIT-101.q: A resident's monthly assessable employment income is VND 15 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-101.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: Bracket 2: 10% × 15 − 0.5 = 1 million. Check: 0.5 (first 10 million × 5%) + 5 × 10% = 1 million VND.

PIT-102.q: A resident's monthly assessable employment income is VND 60 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-102.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: 60 million is the top of bracket 3: 20% × 60 − 3.5 = 8.5 million. Check: 0.5 + 2 + 30 × 20% = 8.5 million VND.

PIT-103.q: October 2026: a chief accountant earns VND 50 million (fully taxable), compulsory insurance 5.25 million, 1 dependant, voluntary pension contribution 3 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-103.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: TI = 50 − 5.25 (insurance) − 15.5 (self) − 6.2 (dependant) − 3 (voluntary pension, at the cap) = 20.05 million (bracket 2). Tax = 10% × 20.05 − 0.5 = 1.505 million VND.

PIT-104.q: A non-resident receives a salary of VND 80 million for work performed in Vietnam in September 2026. What is the PIT (VND)?
PIT-104.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: Non-resident: 80,000,000 × 20% = 16,000,000 VND, no family deductions.
Note: A resident with the same income would pay much less thanks to deductions and the progressive schedule.

PIT-105.q: In 2026 an employee has total taxable salary of VND 300 million, compulsory insurance 25 million, no dependants, and 12 million withheld during the year. At finalisation, how much overpaid tax is refundable or offsettable (VND)?
PIT-105.e: TI = 300 − 25 − 186 = 89 million; annual tax = 89 × 5% = 4.45 million. Overpaid = 12 − 4.45 = 7.55 million VND.
PIT-105.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: TI = 300 − 25 − 186 = 89 million (annual bracket 1 ≤ 120). Annual tax = 89 × 5% = 4.45 million. Withheld 12 → overpaid 7.55 million, refundable or offsettable.
Note: The large gap usually stems from H1 withholding under the old rules.

PIT-106.q: Under Official Letter 7401/CT-QLNT (10/2026), to keep claiming a dependant deduction for a child studying at university, college, vocational secondary school or vocational training, the taxpayer needs:
PIT-106.e: The Tax Department guides that proof of relationship and enrolment are needed; the deduction end month is declared on Form 41/UQ-ĐKT (Circular 90/2026/TT-BTC) and counted in whole months.
o: Documents proving the relationship and documents proving current enrolment
Income confirmation for the child from the tax authority
No documents if the child is under 25
PIT-106.x:
Basis: Tax Department Official Letter 7401/CT-QLNT (10/2026); Circular 90/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: To keep claiming a child over 18 in university, college, vocational training, provide proof of relationship (birth certificate) and current enrolment (school confirmation, student card). The end date is declared on Form 41/UQ-ĐKT.
Distractors: B lacks enrolment proof; C and D have no basis.

PIT-107.q: Under Official Letter 7401/CT-QLNT, the dependant deduction period is counted in whole months.
PIT-107.e: True. Dependant deductions are counted in whole months; the taxpayer declares the start and end months.
PIT-107.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7401/CT-QLNT (10/2026); Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Dependant deductions are counted in whole months: the start and end months each count in full, not pro rata by days.

PIT-108.q: Under Official Letter 7403/CT-TMĐT (10/2026), individuals providing digital content services (games, films, digital photos, music, digital advertising) apply a PIT rate on revenue of:
PIT-108.e: Digital content products and services apply 5% PIT (the same group as asset leasing).
PIT-108.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7403/CT-TMĐT (10/2026); Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Individuals providing digital content (games, films, digital images, music, digital ads) apply a 5% PIT rate on revenue – the same as asset leasing, reflecting high margins.
Distractors: 2% is for ordinary services; 1% and 0.5% are goods distribution groups.

PIT-109.q: Owners of e-commerce platforms with online ordering and payment functions must withhold, file and pay tax on behalf of household/individual businesses selling on the platform.
PIT-109.e: True, under the 2025 Tax Administration Law and Official Letter 7403/CT-TMĐT; if the platform lacks either function, the seller self-declares and pays.
PIT-109.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15; Official Letter 7403/CT-TMĐT (10/2026).
Analysis: True. E-commerce platforms with both online ordering and payment functions must withhold, declare and pay VAT and PIT for household/individual sellers. If either function is missing, sellers file themselves.

PIT-110.q: An individual leases an apartment (not accommodation services) in 2026 with total revenue of VND 1.2 billion and no other business. What PIT is payable (VND million)?
PIT-110.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (amended by Decree 141/2026/ND-CP).
Working: Revenue 1.2 billion > 1 billion threshold. PIT (leasing 5%) per the key is on the excess: (1,200 − 1,000) × 5% = 10 million. VAT 5% on full revenue = 60 million.
Note: PIT on revenue above the threshold is a Decree 141/2026 change; VAT still applies to full revenue once above the threshold.

PIT-111.q: Which of the following is taxable employment income?
PIT-111.e: Responsibility allowances are taxable; SI benefits (sickness, maternity) and lawful overtime pay are not.
o: Sickness benefit paid by the SI fund
PIT-111.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: A monthly responsibility allowance tied to the position is taxable employment income.
Distractors: B and D – sickness and maternity benefits from social insurance aren't taxable; C – compliant overtime is fully exempt from 2026.

PIT-112.q: Select ALL allowances/benefits NOT included in PIT taxable income:
PIT-112.e: Hazard allowances, hardship/accident allowances and SI benefits are not taxable; fixed allowances without regulations and concurrent-position allowances are taxable.
o: Unexpected hardship allowance, occupational accident allowance
Fixed monthly fuel allowance without internal regulations
PIT-112.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Not taxable: (A) prescribed hazard allowances; (B) emergency hardship and work accident allowances; (D) one-off childbirth benefits under social insurance.
Distractors: (C) Lump-sum fuel allowances without a policy and (E) concurrent-position allowances are taxable.

PIT-113.q: November 2026: an employee has base salary of VND 18 million, position allowance 3 million, lawful overtime pay 2.5 million and a cash meal allowance of 1 million; compulsory insurance 2.205 million; no dependants. What is the monthly assessable income (VND)?
PIT-113.e: Taxable income = 18 + 3 = 21 million (overtime exempt, meal allowance ≤ 1.2 million not taxable). TI = 21 − 2.205 − 15.5 = 3.295 million VND.
PIT-113.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Assessable = salary 18 + position allowance 3 = 21 million (overtime 2.5 exempt; meals 1 ≤ 1.2 excluded). TI = 21 − 2.205 − 15.5 = 3.295 million VND.

PIT-114.q: Income payers file PIT monthly or quarterly following their VAT filing period; if no tax is withheld in a period, no withholding return is required for that period.
PIT-114.e: True. If no PIT is withheld in a month/quarter, no return is required for that period.
PIT-114.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Payers file PIT monthly or quarterly (matching the VAT period); a period with no withholding needs no return, but annual finalisation is still required (PIT-059).

PIT-115.q: In 2026 an individual has salary from company A (taxable 360 million, insurance 30 million, 12 million withheld) and casual income of 50 million from company B (10% withheld = 5 million), with 1 dependant all year. On self-finalisation, what is the extra tax (positive) or overpayment (negative) (VND million)?
PIT-115.e: Total taxable income = 360 + 50 = 410; deductions = 30 + 186 + 74.4 = 290.4; TI = 119.6 million → annual tax = 119.6 × 5% = 5.98. Withheld 12 + 5 = 17 → overpaid 11.02 million (−11.02).
PIT-115.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: Assessable = 360 + 50 = 410 million. Deductions = insurance 30 + self 186 + dependant 74.4 = 290.4. TI = 119.6 (≤ 120 → bracket 1). Annual tax = 5.98 million. Withheld 12 + 5 = 17 → overpaid 11.02 million (answer −11.02).
Note: Casual income withheld at 10% is aggregated at finalisation.

PIT-116.q: An individual receives dividends in shares (bonus share issue). When does the 5% PIT obligation arise?
PIT-116.e: Share dividends are not taxed on receipt; on transfer, 5% investment income tax and 0.1% securities transfer tax apply.
o: When the individual transfers those shares
PIT-116.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Stock dividends and bonus shares involve no cash, so no tax on receipt. On sale, the individual pays 5% investment income tax (on par value as regulated) and 0.1% securities transfer tax on the sale price.
Distractors: B, C and D have the wrong timing.

PIT-117.q: An individual wins a VND 15 million lottery prize in October 2026. What PIT is payable (VND)?
PIT-117.e: Below the 20 million per-time threshold, so no tax is payable.
PIT-117.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: 15 million < 20 million threshold (from 01/07/2026) → no tax, answer 0.
Note: Before 01/07/2026, the 10 million threshold would give (15 − 10) × 10% = 0.5 million.

PIT-118.q: Match each income item with its PIT (resident, October 2026):
p: Sale of listed shares for VND 400 million
PIT-118.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: Winnings 70 → (70 − 20) × 10% = 5 million; royalty 40 → (40 − 20) × 5% = 1 million; dividend 40 → 40 × 5% = 2 million (no threshold); shares 400 → 400 × 0.1% = 0.4 million.
Note: Dividends and securities have no 20 million threshold.

PIT-119.q: A foreigner present in Vietnam for 150 days in 2026 but holding a residential lease in Vietnam for 183 days or more in the year may be treated as a tax resident.
PIT-119.e: True. Having a regular residence (including a rented home with a term of 183 days or more in the tax year) is a residence criterion, unless the person proves tax residence of another country.
PIT-119.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Even with under 183 days present, a person with a habitual residence (including a lease of 183 days or more in the tax year) may be resident – unless they prove residence in another country (under a tax treaty).

PIT-120.q: Arrange the payer's steps when paying monthly salary to an employee on a 1-year contract:
PIT-120.e: Withhold using the progressive schedule → file and pay per period → annual finalisation.
o: Compute total income and exclude exempt items
Deduct compulsory insurance and registered family deductions
Apply the progressive schedule and withhold
File PIT for the period (monthly/quarterly) and pay
PIT-120.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: (1) Total income less exempt items → (2) less compulsory insurance and family deductions → (3) apply the schedule and withhold → (4) file and pay monthly/quarterly → (5) finalise annually for delegating employees.

PIT-121.q: Premiums paid by the enterprise for non-savings health insurance for employees are not taxable income.
PIT-121.e: True. Non-compulsory insurance without premium accumulation (health, accident) is not taxable; savings-type products are.
PIT-121.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Non-compulsory, non-accumulating cover (health, personal accident) bought by the employer isn't taxable, as it creates no withdrawable savings. Accumulating policies are taxable (PIT-100).

PIT-122.q: In 2026 a self-finalising individual has eligible medical costs of VND 30 million and domestic master's tuition of 15 million. What is the total deduction (VND million)?
PIT-122.e: Medical capped at 23 (actual 30) → 23; education 15 (≤ 24) → 15. Total 38 million VND.
PIT-122.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Medical: 30 > 23 cap → 23 million. Education: 15 ≤ 24 cap → 15 million. Total 38 million VND.
Note: The caps are separate – unused education room can't absorb medical costs.

PIT-123.q: Consider these statements on PIT taxable income from 01/7/2026:
PIT-123.e: Rent paid on behalf is capped at 15% of total taxable income; in-house meals are not taxable; night pay is fully exempt; internal bonuses are taxable (only certain state awards are exempt).
o: Rent paid by the company on behalf is fully taxable.
Meals cooked by the company for employees are not taxable.
Lawful night-work pay is fully exempt.
PIT-123.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) False – rent paid on behalf is taxable only up to 15% of other taxable income. (2) True – employer-provided meals aren't taxable. (3) True – compliant night pay is fully exempt. (4) False – internal innovation bonuses are taxable; only certain State awards are exempt.

PIT-124.q: A company signs a net salary of VND 40 million/month (PIT borne by the company) with an employee without dependants; grossed-up compulsory insurance is 4.2 million. The grossed-up assessable income is 22.7 million. What is the monthly PIT (VND)?
PIT-124.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: For net salary, gross up to pre-tax income; the given grossed-up TI is 22.7 million (bracket 2). Tax = 10% × 22.7 − 0.5 = 1.77 million VND.
Note: Tax borne by the employer is itself taxable income – hence the gross-up rather than taxing the net pay directly.

PIT-125.q: Individuals' bank deposit interest and interest from life insurance contracts are PIT-exempt.
PIT-125.e: True. These exemptions are retained in Law 109/2025/QH15.
PIT-125.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Bank deposit interest and life insurance interest are exempt – savings incentives retained in the new law.

PIT-126.q: An individual transfers capital contributed to an LLC (not securities). Under PIT rules for capital transfers, tax is computed:
PIT-126.e: Transfers of contributed capital (not securities) are taxed on income (sale price − cost − expenses); securities transfers are taxed at 0.1% of each transfer price.
o: On taxable income (transfer price minus purchase price and costs) at the rate set in Law 109/2025/QH15
PIT-126.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Transfers of non-securities capital stakes are taxed on the gain (price − cost − reasonable expenses) at the statutory rate; securities are taxed at 0.1% of the sale price.
Distractors: B is for securities; C for real estate; D is wrong as it's taxable.

PIT-127.q: A resident's 2026 annual assessable income is VND 1,500 million. What is the annual PIT (VND million)?

PIT-128.q: An individual with taxable salary of VND 15 million/month, compulsory insurance 1.575 million and no dependants pays no PIT.
PIT-128.e: True. 15 − 1.575 − 15.5 < 0, so assessable income is zero.
PIT-128.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: True. 15 − 1.575 − 15.5 = −2.075 < 0 → zero taxable income. With the new deduction, a person without dependants pays only when income after insurance exceeds 15.5 million/month.

PIT-129.q: Select ALL cases where the individual must finalise PIT directly with the tax authority (when there is extra tax payable or a refund requested):
PIT-129.e: Those with a single employer can authorise; the other cases self-finalise to obtain refunds or pay extra.
o: Income from two or more employers, both with 3-month-plus contracts
Has only one 2-year labour contract at one company and authorises finalisation
Has substantial casual income withheld at 10% and wants an overpayment refunded
PIT-129.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Must self-file: (A) two employers with 3-month-plus contracts; (B) claiming medical/education deductions; (D) large casual income withheld at 10% with a refund to claim.
Distractors: (C) A single 2-year contract with one employer can delegate.

PIT-130.q: The resolution adjusting family deductions to VND 15.5 million and 6.2 million/month is:
PIT-130.e: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15 adjusts family deductions from the 2026 tax period.
PIT-130.x:
Basis: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Analysis: The NA Standing Committee's Resolution 110/2025 raised family deductions to 15.5 and 6.2 million/month from 2026.
Distractors: Resolution 204/2025 – VAT reduction; 198/2025 – private sector development; 107/2023 – global minimum tax.

PIT-131.q: December 2026: an employee receives salary of VND 35 million and a 13th-month bonus of 35 million in the same month; compulsory insurance 3.675 million; 1 dependant. What PIT is withheld for December (VND)?
PIT-131.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: The 13th-month bonus paid in December is added to that month: TI = 35 + 35 − 3.675 − 15.5 − 6.2 = 44.625 million (bracket 3). Tax = 20% × 44.625 − 3.5 = 5.425 million VND.
Note: Monthly withholding may be high, but annual finalisation adjusts to total annual income.

PIT-132.q: An individual with overpaid PIT after finalisation may request a refund or offset it against tax payable in the next period.
PIT-132.e: True. Taxpayers choose a refund or offset of overpaid tax under tax administration law.
PIT-132.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. PIT overpaid after finalisation may, at the taxpayer's choice, be refunded (to an account) or offset against later periods.

PIT-133.q: A household retail business has 2026 revenue of VND 2 billion and chooses the percentage-of-revenue method. PIT payable is:
PIT-133.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (amended by Decree 141/2026/ND-CP).
Working: Goods distribution – PIT 0.5% on revenue above the 1 billion threshold: (2,000 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 5 million. VAT 1% on full revenue = 20 million.
Distractors: B applies 0.5% to all revenue; C confuses it with VAT; D is wrong as revenue exceeds the threshold.

PIT-134.q: Remittances received from relatives abroad are PIT-exempt.
PIT-134.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Remittances from relatives abroad are PIT-exempt – a policy encouraging foreign currency inflows.

PIT-135.q: An individual sells a second apartment for VND 4.5 billion (not exempt). What is the PIT (VND million)?
PIT-135.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Working: A second apartment isn't exempt (not the only home): 4,500 × 2% = 90 million VND.

PIT-136.q: Income payers must issue PIT withholding certificates to individuals from whom tax was withheld upon request.
PIT-136.e: True. Withholding certificates (electronic from 01/7/2026) support individuals' finalisation and refunds.
PIT-136.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. PIT withholding certificates (electronic from 01/07/2026) let individuals claim withheld tax at finalisation, request refunds or claim foreign credits.

PIT-137.q: A 20-year-old son studying at university earns an average of VND 2.5 million/month from part-time work. Can the father register him as a dependant for 2026?
PIT-137.e: A child studying at university/college… with average monthly income not exceeding VND 3 million (Decree 253/2026/ND-CP) may be registered as a dependant.
o: Yes, since average income does not exceed VND 3 million/month and he is studying
PIT-137.x:
Basis: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Official Letter 7401/CT-QLNT.
Analysis: Children over 18 in university, college or vocational training with average monthly income up to 3 million qualify as dependants. 2.5 < 3 million → eligible.
Distractors: B ignores the student case; C – income is within the limit; D has no basis.

PIT-138.q: July 2026: a company pays an employee salary of VND 26 million, rent on behalf of 8 million and a cash meal allowance of 1.5 million; insurance 2.73 million; no dependants. What is the monthly assessable income (VND million)?
PIT-138.e: Taxable income excluding rent = 26 + 0.3 (meal allowance above 1.2 million) = 26.3; rent included up to 15% × 26.3 = 3.945 (< 8). TI = 26.3 + 3.945 − 2.73 − 15.5 = 12.015 million VND.
PIT-138.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: (1) Taxable income excluding rent = 26 + 0.3 (meal excess over 1.2) = 26.3. (2) Rent capped at 15% × 26.3 = 3.945 (< 8 paid). (3) TI = 26.3 + 3.945 − 2.73 − 15.5 = 12.015 million VND.
Note: July 2026 uses the 1.2 million meal limit since Decree 253 applies from 01/07/2026.

PIT-139.q: PIT Law 109/2025/QH15 takes effect on 01/7/2026, but the 5-bracket schedule applies to residents' employment income from the 2026 tax period.
PIT-139.e: True. Provisions on residents' employment and business income apply from the 2026 tax period.
PIT-139.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Generally effective 01/07/2026, but residents' employment and business income rules apply from the 2026 period – so the 5-bracket schedule is used for the full-year 2026 finalisation (PIT-001).

PIT-140.q: The deadline for individuals to self-finalise 2026 PIT (the last day of the fourth month is Friday 30/4/2027, a public holiday) is:
PIT-140.e: Individuals finalise by the last day of the fourth month; if it falls on a holiday, the deadline moves to the next working day.
o: The next working day after the holiday
PIT-140.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 148 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: 30/04/2027 is a public holiday (30/4, 1/5 and possibly substitute days), so the deadline moves to the first working day after the break.
Distractors: B contradicts the Civil Code; C is the payer's deadline; D has no basis.

PIT-141.q: Select ALL correct statements on household-business PIT in 2026:
PIT-141.e: Threshold 1 billion (Decree 141/2026); 1–3 billion may choose; over 3–50 billion: 17%; over 50 billion: 20% (income method). Household businesses pay PIT, not CIT.
o: Revenue of VND 1 billion or less pays no PIT
Revenue over 1 to 3 billion may choose the percentage-of-revenue method or the 15% income method
Revenue over 3 to 50 billion is taxed at 17% on taxable income
PIT-141.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (A) True – ≤ 1 billion pays no PIT. (B) True – 1–3 billion may choose percentage of revenue or the income method (15%). (C) True – above 3 to 50 billion pays 17% on taxable income.
Distractors: (D) Household businesses pay PIT, not CIT (CIT-127).

PIT-142.q: Amounts the enterprise spends on employees' training to improve job-related skills are not taxable income of the employees.
PIT-142.e: True. Job-related training is a business expense, not employee income.
PIT-142.x:
Basis: Law 109/2025/QH15; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Job-related training is the company's investment in capability, not employee income. Unlike paying tuition for unrelated personal purposes.

PIT-143.q: A company pays VND 15 million for professional articles to a collaborator without a labour contract (no commitment form). How much PIT is withheld (VND)?
PIT-143.x:
Basis: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
Working: No employment contract, 15 million ≥ 5 million, no commitment form → 15,000,000 × 10% = 1,500,000 VND.

PIT-144.q: An employee who left before the company performs PIT finalisation cannot authorise that company to finalise on their behalf.
PIT-144.e: True. Authorisation requires working for the payer at the time of authorisation (except in corporate reorganisations).
PIT-144.x:
Basis: Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Delegation requires current employment at the payer at the time of delegation (except reorganisations like mergers or conversions). Former employees must self-file if required.

PIT-145.q: The total 2026 annual family deduction for a taxpayer without dependants is:
PIT-145.x:
Basis: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15.
Working: 15.5 × 12 = 186 million VND.
Distractors: 132 million (11 × 12) is the old level; 156 and 200 million have no basis.
